subject: Urgent: PrevailMed AZ congestion causing latency & 5xx — exec bridge requested

From: Lindsey Carrow <lindsey@prevailmed.com>

Cc: Procurement <procure@prevailmed.com>

Subject: Regionally elevated latency + 5xx spike — appearing after routing change

Hi Priyom,

We started seeing elevated p95 latency (2.2s -> 7s) and a rising 5xx rate across our user traffic hitting our northwest AZ deployment about 08:50 PT after the routing adjustment yesterday. Traffic is multi-tenant and we see about 18% failed requests; some customers reported timeouts in their web UI.

Attached is a quick screenshot from our observability dashboard and a small sample of trace IDs. Can you confirm whether Redwood made any routing or model variant changes in that region? This is customer-impacting. We need an immediate timeline for mitigation and any rollback.

Lindsey
Lindsey Carrow

Hi Lindsey — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. We’re seeing correlated telemetry on our side for northwest AZ (az-nw1): p95 jump and increased 5xx across multiple customer tenants.

I’m opening an exec bridge now and pulling in our on-call SRE and capacity leads. Can you share any recent config change IDs from your side? We’ll start by: 1) confirming whether the recent routing policy change introduced a higher-fanout path, 2) checking KV-cache pressure metrics, and 3) preparing an emergency reroute to eastus2 if needed.

ETA for bridge: 20 minutes. I’ll share the bridge dial-in and an initial MAP (mutual action plan) in the next email.

– Priyom

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: PrevailMed — immediate triage plan (internal)

Team — quick context: PrevailMed PV-4491 is seeing a multi-tenant fanout amplification after a routing weight change yesterday afternoon. Our metrics show KV cache saturation and sustained queue growth on the AZ nodes. Business impact: high (several enterprise customers reporting UI failures).

Proposed immediate plan:
- Activate bridge (Priyom will lead comms to customer)
- Fail traffic for PV-4491 to eastus2 (pin to compatible model shard) — roll traffic over in 2 phases (10m then 30m)
- Temporarily disable cross-tenant aggressive prefix caching for that AZ (mitigates KVC pressure)
- Monitor p99 and 5xx; prepare credits if SLA hit confirmed

Please reply with go/no-go. If no objections in 5 min, Rishi execute reroute; Hannah confirm capacity in eastus2.

– Vanessa
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

To: Lindsey Carrow <lindsey@prevailmed.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Regionally elevated latency + 5xx spike — appearing after routing change

Lindsey — we’ve opened an emergency bridge and are initiating a staged reroute to eastus2 now. Rishi and Hannah are driving the cutover; ETA for initial traffic shift is ~20–30 minutes. We will share live monitoring links and a mutual action plan (attached).

Immediate asks for PrevailMed:
- Share any customer-side changes (CDN, ingress) in last 24 hours
- Confirm a single point of contact for procurement if we need to accelerate credits/credits approval

We will track impacts continuously and follow up with a post-incident RCA.

Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: [SRE] Exec note: cause and mitigation actions (internal)

TL;DR: Root cause looks like multi-tenant request amplification after routing weight change combined with KV cache hotspotting. Autoscaler did not react quickly due to queue head-of-line blocking in the inference runtime.

Timeline (observed):
- 08:47 PT: routing weight adjustment increases fanout to az-nw1 for a compatible-but-heavier model shard
- 08:50 PT: p95/p99 begin to rise; queue depth grows rapidly on az nodes
- 09:12 PT: customer alert (Lindsey)
- 09:35 PT: bridge opened; intent to reroute confirmed
- 11:20 PT: staged reroute to eastus2 completed (phase 1) — customer traffic began draining from az-nw1

Immediate SRE mitigations performed:
- Initiated staged reroute to eastus2 (completed phase 1 at 11:20 PT)
- Disabled cross-tenant aggressive prefix caching for az-nw1 to reduce KV pressure
- Adjusted inference runtime queue thresholds to speed autoscaler responsiveness

Current status: p95 down from 7s -> 1.8s; 5xx rate dropping but still above baseline (2.1% currently). We recommend leaving reroute in place for 12–24h while we perform RCA and a controlled repro in staging.

Action items for product/ops:
- Coordinate an RCA and a follow-up test plan (Hannah)
- Draft customer credit recommendation (CS/Sales)
- Create a postmortem and publish within 72h

– Rishi
SRE Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Lindsey Carrow <lindsey@prevailmed.com>, Procurement <procure@prevailmed.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regionally elevated latency + 5xx spike — appearing after routing change

Lindsey / Prevail team — quick status and next steps: 

1) Current state: we completed a staged reroute to eastus2 (phase 1) at 11:20 PT. Observed p95 improved to ~1.8s and 5xx rate is falling (now ~2.1%). We’ll keep traffic pinned while we complete the RCA.

2) Root cause (short): routing weight change caused higher request fanout to a heavier model shard in az-nw1, which amplified cache pressure and triggered queueing in our inference runtime. Rishi’s team performed mitigations (disable aggressive prefix caching, runtime threshold changes). Full RCA to follow.

3) Compensation/credits: Marissa/CS — recommend a prorated service credit for the impacted window (we estimate ~3 hours of elevated error/latency for PV-4491). Marissa — can you confirm recommended amount so procurement can sign-off?

4) Next steps:
- RCA and postmortem (72h) — Rishi/Hannah to lead
- Joint repro test in staging (24–48h) before re-introducing previous routing weights
- Exec sync tomorrow 10:00 PT to review credit and broader preventive actions

Thanks for the quick collaboration and apologies for the impact. We’ll follow up with the MAP link and the full post-incident timeline.

– Priyom
Account Executive, Customer Escalations — Redwood Inference
